title: 9 links that explain today's global ETF moves. Southeast Asia is down10% this quarter — bargain or trap?
author: tickeron_community
selftext:
Singapore's ETF is down 5.6% in a month and Southeast Asia's is off  
about 10% for the quarter. Today's international matchups: CQQQ vs  
MCHI for China, EWZ vs FLBR for Brazil, and two emerging-markets  
funds. Plus a direct play on the Japanese yen. Here's today's world  
tour of the international ETF moves that stood out.  
  
Here is the rundown, drawn from today's write-ups.  
  
\*\*1. iShares MSCI Singapore ETF (EWS)\*\* — EWS is a passively managed  
exchange-traded fund (ETF) that tracks the MSCI Singapore 25/50 Index,  
providing exposure to large- and mid-capitalization companies listed  
in Singapore.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/ishares-msci-singapore-etf-ews-shows-5-6-decline-over-30-days-in-concentrated-banking-exposure-39454/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/ishares-msci-singapore-etf-ews-shows-5-6-decline-over-30-days-in-concentrated-banking-exposure-39454/)  
  
\*\*2. Global X FTSE Southeast Asia ETF (ASEA)\*\* — ASEA tracks the  
FTSE/ASEAN 40 Index, providing passive, rules-based exposure to 40 of  
the largest and most liquid companies across Singapore, Malaysia,  
Indonesia, Thailand, and the Philippines.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/global-x-ftse-southeast-asia-etf-asea-analyzing-the-recent-3-monthly-and-10-quarterly-moves-39467/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/global-x-ftse-southeast-asia-etf-asea-analyzing-the-recent-3-monthly-and-10-quarterly-moves-39467/)  
  
\*\*3. CQQQ vs MCHI\*\* — Tech Concentration or Broad China Exposure –  
Which Fits Your Portfolio?. Two setups, one head-to-head. Which one  
comes out ahead? The breakdown is in the link.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/cqqq-vs-mchi-tech-concentration-or-broad-china-exposure-which-fits-your-portfolio-39524/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/cqqq-vs-mchi-tech-concentration-or-broad-china-exposure-which-fits-your-portfolio-39524/)

Brazil ETFs. Two setups, one head-to-head. Which one comes out ahead?  
The breakdown is in the link.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/ewz-vs-flbr-weighing-cost-efficiency-against-liquidity-in-brazil-etfs-39546/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/ewz-vs-flbr-weighing-cost-efficiency-against-liquidity-in-brazil-etfs-39546/)

[https://tickeron.com/blogs/idub-etf-international-exposure-paired-with-an-enhanced-yield-approach-39613/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/idub-etf-international-exposure-paired-with-an-enhanced-yield-approach-39613/)  
  
\*\*9. Pacer Industrials and Logistics ETF (SHPP)\*\* — The $38 central  
target is drawn from public price-objective data, not a direct analyst  
consensus on the ETF itself. TipRanks aggregates the 12-month analyst  
price targets of SHPP's underlying holdings at an average of about  
$38.06, with a range from roughly $28.82 to $43.80. Target, not a  
promise.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/pacer-industrials-and-logistics-etf-shpp-path-to-38-39468/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/pacer-industrials-and-logistics-etf-shpp-path-to-38-39468/)

Not financial advice. Figures are from today's (Nov 17) write-ups,  
using intraday or latest-close prices, not live quotes. Price targets
